newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Aug natgas prices gain on weather, nukes--NGC.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Aug natgas prices gain on weather, nukes--NGC.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices edged up slightly for August, boosted by expectations for more hot weather this month and continued nuclear plant outages across the country, Natural Gas Clearinghouse (NGC) said in its monthly survey.
U.S. spot gas prices for August averaged $2.07 per million British thermal units, up four cents from July's average of $2.03 but six cents under last August's average, NGC said.
The largest monthly gain was on Houston Pipeline, where prices firmed 10 cents for the month to $2.15, still off 10 cents from year-ago levels.
Most Gulf pipes were steady to five cents higher on the month but were still five to 10 cents below last year.
Prices into Columbia Gas rose five cents from July to $2.15, 10 cents below 1996 levels, NGC said.
Prices on Oklahoma pipes also gained about five cents, with ANR in Custer County quoted at $2.05, up from July's $2.00 but still a nickel below last year.

Prices represent NGC estimates of the median price for one month spot transactions at the indicated receipt points. The estimates are based upon quotes by industial end-users and local distribution companies, NGC said.
